Article Title: In 2021, Vishal Garg, CEO of $7 billion company fired 900 people on Zoom call; five years later he has been sacked; read 'termination letter'
Article Text:
Representative Image

When Vishal Garg fired 900 employees on a Zoom call, just days before Christmas break

What Better Home & Finance Holding said on Vishal Garg's termination

Vishal Garg sends letter to shareholder asking them to get his CEO job back

US-based Better Home & Finance Holding Company has announced that it terminated founder Vishal Garg as CEO and accused him of delaying the company’s quarterly filing, sharply escalating a dispute over control of the mortgage lender. The statement comes just a day after Garg demanded that five directors resign and claimed majority shareholder support for the proposed board overhaul. Better said that every director other than Garg unanimously voted to terminate him after developing concerns about his "judgment, temperament and credibility."The board also accused Garg of refusing to follow the company’s established shareholder-governance process and said that it would not voluntarily return control to him. Incidentally, the statement contradicts Better’s August 3 announcement that Garg had “mutually agreed” with the board to transition out of the CEO role.In December 201, just days before Christmas, Garg made headlines for laying off 900 employees during a Zoom call. More precisely, on December 6, 2021, Garg announced that the mortgage company is laying off about 9% of its workforce during a Zoom webinar, abruptly informing the more than 900 employees on the call.“If you’re on this call, you are part of the unlucky group that is being laid off,” Garg said on the call. “Your employment here is terminated effective immediately. ” He then said employees could expect an email from HR detailing benefits and severance.Garg cited market efficiency, performance and productivity as the reason behind the firings. The episode also included a leaked email in which Garg referred to employees as “dumb dolphins.” “You are TOO DAMN SLOW. You are a bunch of DUMB DOLPHINS… SO STOP IT. STOP IT. STOP IT RIGHT NOW. YOU ARE EMBARRASSING ME,” Garg reportedly wrote. He subsequently took a monthlong leave while Better’s board commissioned a leadership and cultural assessment, then returned as CEO in January 2022.The Board of Directors (the “Board”), excluding Mr. Garg, unanimously voted to terminate Mr. Garg as Chief Executive Officer following a series of decisions and actions that raised serious concerns regarding his judgment, temperament and credibility. Together with Mr. Garg’s track record—including cumulative GAAP net losses exceeding $1.5 billion since 2022 and a stock price that had declined more than 90% under his leadership—the Board concluded that Mr. Garg was no longer fit to serve in an executive capacity at the Company.Mr. Garg himself told the Board that the Company would have been better off had the capital raised under his leadership simply been invested in U.S. Treasury securities rather than deployed under his stewardship.To get his job back, Garg has hired the high-profile lawyer Alex Spiro, partner at Quinn Emanuel, to represent him. He has also sent a letter to the board demanding it return him as CEO. He says that he will work for $1 a year until he returns the company to profitability, and that he will transition out of the CEO role afterwards. “It’s an acknowledgment that I’ve been doing this for 10 years, but execution hasn’t been perfect,” Garg said. “I hope it gets resolved. I think the future still remains very bright for Better,” Garg wrote in the letter.
Article Summary: Better Home & Finance Holding Company terminated founder Vishal Garg as CEO. The statement comes just a day after Garg demanded that five directors resign. In December 201, just days before Christmas, Garg made headlines for laying off 900 employees during a Zoom call.

Article Title: In 1830s, real estate agents used Cosmorama gallery to give wealthy 'virtual walkthrough' of fancy mansions; here's how technology worked
Article Text:
Cosmorama Technology (AI-generated image for representational purpose)

Why cosmorama technology worked for real estate

How real estate agents used cosmoramas

Decades ago, rich homebuyers viewed properties through a certain lens. In the 1830s, London estate agents used a technology called the cosmorama to give wealthy buyers a form of “virtual walkthrough” of mansions and country estates. A new study published in the journal Early Popular Visual Culture found evidence that the technology was being used for commercial real estate listings as early as 1838.​The cosmorama allowed prospective buyers to view magnified and illuminated paintings of properties and their surrounding grounds through a lens. Estate agents Brooks and Hedger, later known as Brooks and Green, advertised these cosmoramic views as a way for buyers to inspect distant properties without immediately travelling to them.​“Its great advantages over mere verbal description, is that a purchaser, intent on visiting a distant property may thus enjoy the advantage of having it brought, as it were, within his view, or of selecting for inspection from amongst many, that which best suits his taste and fortune,” one newspaper advertisement said.Cosmoramas emerged in Paris in 1808 and became more widely used during the 1820s. The displays typically consisted of detailed paintings that viewers examined through magnifying lenses.The lens altered how the images appeared, creating a sense of depth and allowing viewers to see distant locations in greater detail.​The technology was primarily used for visual entertainment. People could use cosmoramas to view scenes of cities, landscapes and places far from their homes. The format offered a way to see locations that many viewers would otherwise have been unable to visit.John Plunkett, a professor at the University of Exeter and co-author of the study, was researching 19th-century English cosmoramas when he found a newspaper advertisement from Brooks and Hedger dated to 1838. The estate agency said it offered cosmoramic views of properties available for sale.The advertisements described views showing mansions and their surrounding estates from a bird’s-eye perspective. Creating the images required artists to visit the properties and paint the scenes by hand before they could be displayed through the cosmorama.Brooks and Hedger continued offering the service for nearly two decades, with most of the advertisements found by Plunkett dating from the 1840s. One advertisement described a property view as showing the mansion and estate with “all the vividness and truth of nature.”Because producing each image required considerable work, the service was aimed at expensive properties and country estates.The use of cosmoramas for property sales coincided with changes in the 19th-century real estate market. Population growth and urbanisation increased demand for property, while improvements in transport made it easier for people to travel between locations.The emergence of specialised estate agents also changed how properties were marketed. Instead of relying only on written descriptions, agents could use visual material to show prospective buyers what a distant property looked like.Plunkett said the commercial use of cosmoramas showed how the technology could be adapted beyond entertainment.“What we’ve discovered through this latest research project, however, is that its use extended beyond simple entertainment: the appeal of cosmoramas was that they sold an experience of virtual travel,” Plunkett said in a statement. “This was utilised by estate agents seeking to sell luxury properties and country estates.”The property advertisements therefore provided an early example of estate agents using visual technology to let prospective buyers examine properties remotely. The approach predates modern online listings, panoramic images and virtual reality tours by more than a century.“But the founding of the first specialised estate agents set in motion a more professional approach to marketing property, fuelled by population growth, urbanisation and improved transport links,” Plunkett added. “In that context, we can see how Brooks and Green pioneered the virtual tour, over 150 years before digital technology would fully realise this potential.”
Article Summary: The cosmorama allowed prospective buyers to view magnified and illuminated paintings of properties and their surrounding grounds through a lens. Estate agents Brooks and Hedger, later known as Brooks and Green, advertised these cosmoramic views as a way for buyers to inspect distant properties without immediately travelling to them.

Article Title: SpaceX closes $60 billion Cursor deal: CEO Elon Musk calls it ‘honour’
Article Text:
Here is Cursor’s full announcement

Cursor has officially been acquired by SpaceX. This completes the acquisition process that started in April, when we announced our partnership with SpaceXAI to accelerate our model training efforts.

In the years since we started Cursor, better models have steadily expanded what people can build. Cursor has gone from completing the next few lines of code to building AI teammates that you can give real work to.

Together with SpaceX, we will push that ambition further. We will have access to the largest fleet of GPUs in the world, giving us the compute to build stronger models that are also more economical to run.

This means we can provide customers with more capable models at lower cost. Grok 4.6, which we released Wednesday, provides an early look at what we can now build together. SpaceX is building the computing capacity needed to scale intelligence far beyond what exists today. Cursor will be one place where that intelligence becomes useful.

For us, that opens a much larger horizon than the one we started with, while keeping the work familiar. We still want to help people with ambitious ideas spend less time writing code and more time solving harder problems.
Article Summary: Cursor has officially been acquired by SpaceX. This completes the acquisition process that started in April. Cursor has gone from completing the next few lines of code to building AI teammates that you can give real work to. SpaceX is building the computing capacity needed to scale intelligence.

Article Title: Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath to startup founders: Stop saying 'we use AI'; 'Bragging that your product uses AI is like …’
Article Text:
Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath

Nithin Kamath says AI is now 'table stakes'

'Opening your pitch with AI' may hurt startup founders

Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath has shared a post with a message for startup founders trying to impress investors with AI. In a post on X, Nithin Kamath said he has become tired of seeing investment pitch decks that begin by highlighting AI, arguing that using AI is no longer a unique selling point. According to Kamath, AI has become so common that leading a presentation with "we use AI" is more likely to turn investors away than attract them. He said that “bragging that your product uses AI is like bragging that you take a bath every day”.Sharing his views, Kamath said the number of startup presentations that begin by talking about AI has become excessive. "The number of investment decks I get leading with 'we use AI' is ridiculous. It's reached a point where it automatically makes my eyes roll, and I've almost stopped looking at them," Kamath wrote.He said founders should understand that AI is no longer a competitive advantage by itself. "Founders need to realize that AI is just table stakes now. Bragging that your product uses AI is like bragging that you take a bath every day. It's not a differentiator."According to Kamath, simply saying a product uses AI does not explain why customers or investors should care.In the post, Nithin Kamath warned that making AI the first thing investors hear could have the opposite effect. "In fact, opening your pitch with it is a surefire way to get ignored, not just by us, but by most serious VCs," he said.Kamath also pointed to another trend created by generative AI. He said AI tools have made it easier than ever for founders to create polished-looking presentations, but that has also made many startup pitches look and sound alike."Especially now that AI has democratized the ability to generate 'nice-looking' decks, the last thing you want to do is say the exact same generic things as every other founder using the exact same tools," he wrote.
Article Summary: Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath says AI is no longer a unique selling point. Leading a presentation with "we use AI" is more likely to turn investors away than attract them. Kamath: Bragging that your product uses AI is like bragging that you take a bath every day.

Article Title: France’s top court blocks social media ban for kids: Here is what the ruling said
Article Text:
Representative image

Concerns cited over privacy and age verification

France’s highest constitutional authority on Friday (August 14) struck down landmark legislation aimed at banning teenagers under the age of 15 from using social media platforms, ruling that the proposed restrictions disproportionately infringed upon constitutional rights to free expression and privacy. The decision delivers a notable setback to President Emmanuel Macron’s administration, which has prioritised tightening youth digital safety rules and reducing screen time among minors.According to a report by news agency Reuters, following the ruling, the Elysee Palace announced that Macron has instructed Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu to redraft the bill to address the court's constitutional concerns before the end of his term in early 2027.The contested legislation, passed by French lawmakers in July, would have prohibited minors under 15 from creating new accounts on platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, Snapchat and YouTube starting September 1. Additionally, the rules required tech companies to terminate existing accounts held by underage users within four months and mandate identity-based age verification mechanisms approved by France’s data privacy regulator.However, the Constitutional Council concluded that the measure failed to provide adequate statutory safeguards, saying that the broad prohibition excessively curtailed the constitutional freedom of communication and expression for young citizens. The Justices also noted that while the bill required all internet users to submit age verification, it did not define the strict conditions, legal limits and data protection boundaries required to protect personal privacy.“The Council holds that the contested provisions, on the one hand, disproportionately infringe upon the freedom of expression and communication and, on the other, fail to provide the legal safeguards necessary to ensure the right to respect for private life,” the ruling stated.The French initiative was part of a widening international movement to restrict youth access to algorithm-driven social feeds. Lawmakers in Paris sought to follow Australia, which passed a nationwide ban for minors under 16 in December, while regulators in China, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates and the European Union continue to introduce stricter age verification frameworks and child safety regulations.
Article Summary: France's highest constitutional authority struck down landmark legislation aimed at banning teenagers under the age of 15 from using social media platforms. The decision delivers a notable setback to President Emmanuel Macron’s administration, which has prioritised tightening youth digital safety rules and reducing screen time among minors.

Article Title: China’s Z.ai claims its new GLM-5.3 model is close to Anthropic’s Mythos 5 level in cybersecurity tests
Article Text:
Representative image

Tiered rollout and responsible disclosure

Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) startup Z.ai has announced that its upcoming open-source model, GLM-5.3, demonstrated vulnerability detection capabilities on par with Anthropic’s restricted cybersecurity model, Mythos 5. Citing internal benchmark data shared by the company, a news article by Reuters says that GLM-5.3 scored 84.5% on CyberGym, which is an industry benchmark evaluating a model's ability to review source code, detect security flaws, and verify their authenticity. In comparison, Z.ai reported an 83.8% score for Anthropic's Mythos 5.While the model showed parity in passive flaw detection, it trailed Anthropic’s model in active exploit generation. On the ExploitBench test, GLM-5.3 achieved a 54.4% score versus 78% for Mythos 5. In timed tests, GLM-5.3 completed 130 attack-development tasks over six hours, compared to 247 tasks logged by Mythos 5.Anthropic currently restricts access to Mythos—a specialized derivative of Claude Fable 5 with offensive safety guardrails removed, limiting deployment strictly to vetted corporate and institutional partners under its "Project Glasswing" initiative.Taking a hybrid approach, Z.ai stated it plans a public release of GLM-5.3 in roughly two weeks following safety audits. However, the startup confirmed that its most sensitive cybersecurity capabilities will remain restricted behind a "trusted access" vetting program for launch partners.Industry governance analysts pointed to the structured rollout as a milestone for domestic risk management."To the best of my knowledge, this is the first time a Chinese lab is publicly justifying a delayed open release of model weights with safety considerations. This shows that open-weight risk management practices in China are becoming more sophisticated,” said Gabriel Wagner, an AI governance researcher at Beijing-based consultancy Concordia AI.To prevent misuse, Z.ai added multi-layered guardrails to screen incoming prompts and train the system to refuse malicious requests while preserving functionality for authorized penetration testing and bug fixing.
Article Summary: Z.ai's GLM-5.3 demonstrated vulnerability detection capabilities on par with Anthropic’s restricted cybersecurity model, Mythos 5. Anthropic currently restricts access to Mythos with offensive safety guardrails removed, limiting deployment strictly to vetted corporate and institutional partners under its "Project Glasswing" initiative.

Article Title: Can I use soapy water to clean TV screen? Here’s what you should know
Article Text:
Tips to to clean TV screen safely (AI-generated image)

How to clean TV screen safely with soap

Dip a clean microfiber cloth into the solution

Wring it out thoroughly so it is only slightly damp.

Wipe the screen gently using light, circular motions without pressing hard.

Once clean, use a dry microfiber cloth to remove any remaining moisture.

Things that you should never use to clean your TV screen

Never use glass cleaner on a TV screen

Avoid paper towels

Don't use household cleaning sprays

Skip rubbing alcohol and harsh chemicals

Never spray water directly on the screen

Don't use rough cloths or old rags

Avoid excessive pressure while cleaning

Avoid baby wipes or wet wipes

Don't use abrasive sponges or scrubbers

Cleaning a TV screen looks like a simple job, but the wrong product or tool can scratch the display, strip its protective coating, or cause permanent damage. Modern LED, OLED, QLED and Mini-LED televisions come with delicate anti-glare and anti-reflective coatings that need careful handling. One question often asked is whether one can use soapy water to clean a TV screen? The short answer is: not directly. While a small amount of diluted soapy water may be recommended for stubborn stains, using too much soap, spraying liquid directly on the display, can damage the screen's protective coating or allow moisture to seep inside the TV.If you need to remove stubborn fingerprints or greasy marks, use only a very small amount of mild dish soap mixed with distilled water.Note: Avoid using strong detergents or excess soap, as they can damage the screen's protective coating.Experts say only approved cleaning methods should be used, and have flagged several household items that people commonly reach for by mistake. Here's a look at what to avoid when cleaning your TV screen, and why.Most glass cleaners contain ammonia, alcohol or other harsh chemicals that can damage the protective coating on modern displays.These products may work fine on windows or mirrors, but on a TV screen they can leave streaks and permanently alter its finish.Paper towels may feel soft, but they contain wood fibres that can scratch the screen over time. Addiitnally, they can also leave lint behind, making the display look dirtier after cleaning.Multi-purpose cleaners, kitchen cleaners and disinfectant sprays are not designed for electronics. Spraying them directly on the TV can damage its screen and may allow liquid to seep into the edges of the screen.Strong cleaning agents such as rubbing alcohol, acetone, bleach or ammonia-based products can strip away the anti-reflective coating found on many modern televisions. Once damaged, the coating cannot be restored.Water sprayed onto a display can run down and seep into the TV through its edges or vents, raising the risk of internal damage. If moisture is needed, a lightly dampened microfiber cloth is the safer route.Old T-shirts, towels, tissues and rough fabric can carry dirt or coarse fibres that scratch the display. A clean microfiber cloth remains the safest choice for wiping away dust and fingerprints.Pressing hard on the screen can damage the display panel, especially on OLED and LED TVs. Use light, gentle strokes instead of scrubbing stubborn marks.Wet wipes or for that matter baby wipes contain cleaning chemicals, fragrances or moisturisers that are not safe for TV screens. Using wet wipes on screen can leave residue and may damage the coating over time.Kitchen sponges, scouring pads or abrasive cleaning tools can permanently scratch the TV screen, even with gentle use. These products should never be used on electronic displays.
Article Summary: Cleaning a TV screen looks like a simple job, but the wrong product or tool can scratch the display, strip its protective coating, or cause permanent damage. Experts say only approved cleaning methods should be used, and have flagged several household items that people commonly reach for by mistake.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg and Merab Dvalishvili go 'fighting' in the middle of the sea, Meta CEO shares one-minute-plus video says: Merab made me ...
Article Text:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg: ‘Merab made me take my shirt off’

Mark Zuckerberg’s well-known MMA habit

The yacht controversy

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has taken his mixed martial arts training to new heights or rather new waters by sparring with former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili on a giant barge in the middle of Lake Tahoe. In a one-minute-plus video shared on Instagram, the pair traded blows in front of drones, videographers, and friends, with Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan casually paddling past on a canoe.Zuckerberg also joked in the one-minute clip that Dvalishvili insisted that he remove his shirt ‘because it looks more fighter.’ While the UFC star appeared to be going easy on the billionaire, Zuckerberg showcased striking and wrestling skills, even throwing Dvalishvili into the water. The sparring session marks the second time the duo have trained together, following a December 2025 meet-up.The footage captured multiple angles of the sparring rounds, with an array of cameras clearly set up in advance to document the encounter. At one point, Zuckerberg's wife Priscilla Chan is seen paddling past the barge on a canoe. Sharing the clip, Zuckerberg explained that Dvalishvili had told him to take his shirt off because it looks more fighter.Dvalishvili, who won the UFC bantamweight title in 2024 and remains the division's top contender, appeared to go easy on the tech billionaire throughout the session. Even so, Zuckerberg got a moment to show off his striking and wrestling, at one point throwing Dvalishvili into the lake. This marks the second time the pair have sparred publicly, having first done rounds together in December 2025.Zuckerberg has built a reputation over the past few years for training regularly in MMA and jiujitsu, often sparring with some of the sport's most accomplished fighters. His dedication to the sport previously prompted UFC president Dana White to remark that the Meta boss could hold his own physically against just about anyone.The viral fight comes as Zuckerberg faces scrutiny over his $300 million yacht Launchpad, which was accused of ignoring a distress call from a stranded vessel in Alaskan waters earlier this month. Mark Zuckerberg’s $390 million, 387-foot yacht Launchpad was recently booed over a reported failure to respond to a stranded boat. A Meta spokesperson has now clarified that the vessel's crew was on a different radio channel and that help was already on the way. The incident happened last Monday, August 3 evening in Alaska after a 21-foot skiff ran out of fuel between Juneau and Petersburg. While social media users criticised Mark Zuckerberg's superyacht, the company said neither Zuckerberg nor his family were on board at the time.
Article Summary: Mark Zuckerberg sparred with former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili on a giant barge in the middle of Lake Tahoe. The pair traded blows in front of drones, videographers, and friends, with Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan casually paddling past on a canoe. Zuckerberg has built a reputation for training regularly in MMA and jiujitsu, often sparring with some of the sport's most accomplished fighters.

Article Title: Nick Long, Mayor of League City in Texas, joins H-1B visa debate; says: H-1B program should not be used by any ...
Article Text:
The debate began after Texas State University filed a notice of intent to sponsor an H-1B visa for a Public Relations Specialist position

Public universities are H-1B cap-exempt

Nick Long, Mayor of League City in Texas has joined the H-1b visa debate publicly. Long recently said in an X post that no public organisation should use the H-1B program, arguing taxpayer-funded jobs should go to taxpayers in response to Texas State University's filing for a Public Relations Specialist role. Nick Long’s comments came in response to a post announcing that the Texas State University (@txst) has filed a notice of intent to hire an H-1B Public Relations administrator.The debate began after Texas State University filed a notice of intent to sponsor an H-1B visa for a Public Relations Specialist position. The filing prompted Scott Bowen, Republican nominee for Texas House of Representatives, to share the post on his timeline writing: “Texas State graduates hundreds of communication majors every year. Not one of them was qualified for this job?”.Nick Long quoted the post and wrote: “No public entity should be using H-1B program. Taxpayers should get taxpayer funded jobs”.Under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA § 214(g)(5)(A) and (B)), certain categories of H1B petitions are exempt from the annual numerical cap of 65,000 (plus 20,000 master's cap). This means they can sponsor eligible foreign workers for H-1B visas throughout the year without participating in the annual lottery.The exemption also applies to nonprofit entities affiliated with higher education institutions and certain nonprofit or government research organisations.In other news, a new research indicates a projected decline in international student enrollment for Fall 2026. Preliminary analysis by NAFSA: Association of International Educators and JB International shows cascading effects on US economic contribution and jobs supported. This downturn reflects the convergence of several headwinds: declining application volumes, persistent visa appointment bottlenecks, and newly restrictive immigration policy changes.
Article Summary: The debate began after Texas State University filed a notice of intent to sponsor an H-1B visa for a Public Relations Specialist position. Nick Long quoted the post and wrote: “No public entity should be using H- 1B program. Taxpayers should get taxpayer funded jobs’

Article Title: Few years ago, US store owner found 97 ultra rare vintage Mario game cartridges: They are now up for auction
Article Text:
A casual scrap-metal purchase turns into a ‘Holy Grail’

Cassettes get record-breaking grades from authenticators

Auction details and charity announcement

A box of 97 factory-fresh vintage Nintendo video games that sat untouched in a US storage for years has officially hit the auction block, putting one of the most unusual discoveries in retro gaming history up for public bidding on Friday (August 14). According to a report, this collection consists of 97 uncirculated copies of the classic Super Mario Bros. / Duck Hunt combination cartridge. Originally released for the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) in 1988, these specific copies carry a 1993 manufacturing date – two years after the title was thought to be discontinued, essentially making them the last known production run and a previously undocumented variant in gaming archives. The online sale began through Goldin's Pop Culture Auction and will run through September 9.The discovery was made when Kevin Braun, owner of One Stop Wonders in Waukesha, Wisconsin, asked long-time Nintendo collector and Nintendo Wire founder Jason Ganos to help appraise and sell common games and Pokémon cards. During the conversation, Braun brought up a forgotten box of cartridges he had previously bought from a customer whose family originally saved them for scrap metal.When Ganos examined the games, he discovered that all 97 copies were in flawless, unplayed condition. As Nintendo officially ended standard production of the combination bundle in 1991, collectors believe this unexpected 1993 batch was produced either as warranty replacement inventory or for a retail store promotion that never made it to shelves.Realising the potential value of the uncirculated batch, Ganos personally transported all 97 game cartridges in his carry-on luggage to California for professional authentication and grading. Examiners at Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA) graded the entire batch, awarding five of the 97 cartridges a flawless “Gem Mint 10.” According to Ganos, PSA had never previously awarded a perfect 10 grade to an original NES cartridge.While high-grade vintage video games have commanded six-figure sums in recent years, Ganos noted that it is difficult to predict the final hammer price because uncirculated, high-graded NES cartridges with this specific production history have never appeared on the public market before.Braun and Ganos are offering the majority of the cartridges in the current sale, including three of the five copies awarded the historic perfect 10 grade. Both men are retaining one perfect-grade copy each alongside select high 9-rated copies for their personal collections.
Article Summary: A box of 97 factory-fresh vintage Nintendo video games has officially hit the auction block. The collection consists of 97 uncirculated copies of the classic Super Mario Bros. / Duck Hunt combination cartridge. These specific copies carry a 1993 manufacturing date – two years after the title was thought to be discontinued. Article Title: Microsoft is ‘killing’ Mico, the Copilot mascot it launched last October
Article Text:
Microsoft killed Clippy once. It's just done it again with Mico

Clippy survived a decade. Mico didn't last a year

Group Chat, Podcasts and Deep Research die on August 18 too

Microsoft is pulling Mico, the animated yellow blob that has fronted Copilot Voice since last October, out of the assistant's voice mode. The character isn't being deleted outright—it's being shifted to Learn Live, Microsoft's voice-based study mode, where it will work as an animated tutor. Copilot Voice itself stays exactly where it is. You'll still be able to talk to the chatbot and get spoken replies. You just won't have a blob pulling faces at you while you do it.The change was spotted on a Microsoft support page and reported by The Verge, and it lands as part of a much bigger housekeeping exercise. Microsoft is merging its consumer Copilot app with the Microsoft 365 Copilot app, and account updates begin rolling out from August 18, 2026. Mico goes in waves rather than on a single date, so your account may lose it before or after someone else's.Mico arrived in the Copilot Fall Release in October 2025, with Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman positioning it as a way to give the assistant an identity. It changed colour, reacted in real time, and was meant to make voice conversations feel less like talking to a spreadsheet. Microsoft's support page now says the character taught it about warmth, expressiveness, and how people want to talk with AI, and that Learn is where it has the most room to grow.That puts Mico in familiar company. Clippy shipped with Office 97 and was gone by Office 2007. Cortana ran from 2014 until its standalone app was retired in 2023. Rover and Bob went the same way in the nineties.Mico isn't the only casualty. Group Chat, Podcasts, Copilot Labs and consumer Deep Research all retire that day. Paid professional users get a tool called Researcher in place of Deep Research.There's a small amount of homework here. Existing Group Chats migrate as individual conversations, but messages, images and files uploaded by other participants won't come across, so download anything you want to keep first. Podcasts can be saved individually before the cutoff. And if you spent time customising your Mico's colours and looks, Microsoft's advice: take a screenshot, because those settings don't travel to Learn Live.
Article Summary: Mico, the animated yellow blob that has fronted Copilot Voice since last October, is being moved to Learn Live, Microsoft's voice-based study mode. Group Chat, Podcasts, Copilot Labs and consumer Deep Research all retire on August 18, 2026.

Article Title: US government announces 100% tariff on Chinese drone technology; says: We have closed the backdoor that…
Article Text:
Trump administration is closing the supply-chain loophole

Trump administration slaps tariffs on allies

US President Donald Trump has introduced a sweeping tariff package on imported drones and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) components, aiming to eliminate reliance on Chinese hardware across commercial sectors, law enforcement agencies and local governments. Under the new directives announced by the White House, the US will impose a 100% tariff on drone systems classified as “particularly sensitive” to national security. According to a report by The Financial Times, this tier covers systems that feature thermal imaging sensors or have an overall weight exceeding 25 kilograms. Lighter consumer and commercial units with a maximum takeoff weight under 25 kilograms will face a 255 levy.Trade and national security analysts highlighted that the latest measure targets component-level imports to prevent domestic assembly workarounds. Craig Singleton, a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, described the tariffs as a major intervention that closes an operational gap left after earlier import bans.“It still primarily targets China, but it's designed to stop supply-chain laundering,” Singleton was quoted as saying, noting that the rules close a backdoor that previously allowed domestic firms to import millions of Chinese motors, rotors, and airframes to assemble domestically.Singleton added that the policy will require US commercial and public-sector buyers to undertake an immediate, capital-intensive pivot toward suppliers based domestically or in allied nations, even if unit costs are significantly higher.The latest action follows a December order by the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) that barred wireless communications approvals for drones manufactured by foreign adversary nations.Alongside direct measures, the White House accused more than 40 countries of assisting Chinese manufacturers in bypassing existing trade rules by rerouting technology products through third-party jurisdictions. To encourage sourcing through secure supply lines, the administration established preferential tariff tiers for allied nations.The US government has applied a 10% tariff to drone hardware and technology imported from the UK. Similarly, it applied a 15% tariff to equipment imported from the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland and Liechtenstein.To build domestic manufacturing capacity, the executive order directs the US Department of Commerce to launch a dedicated onshoring program providing support for companies investing in domestic UAV development and supply-chain manufacturing.
Article Summary: The US will impose a 100% tariff on drone systems classified as ‘particularly sensitive’ to national security. Lighter consumer and commercial units with a maximum takeoff weight under 25 kilograms will face a 255 levy. To encourage sourcing through secure supply lines, the administration established preferential tariff tiers for allied nations.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Bill Gates: “Your most unhappy customers are your greatest source of…” - the surprising lesson hidden in every complaint
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Bill Gates

“Your most unhappy customers are your greatest source of learning.”

Understanding the meaning of the quote by Bill Gates

Why unhappy customers can provide useful information

All about Bill Gates and his approach to business

What businesses can learn from complaints

The lesson beyond customer service

Why the quote still matters

Lessons learnt from Bill Gates’ quote

Listen to criticism carefully. Negative feedback can reveal problems that are easy to overlook from inside a business or organisation.

Look for patterns, not isolated complaints. One unhappy customer may have had an unusual experience, but repeated complaints can point to a wider weakness.

Fix the cause, not just the immediate problem. Offering a refund or apology may settle one case, while correcting the underlying issue can prevent similar complaints later.

Do not dismiss uncomfortable feedback. Criticism can be difficult to hear, but discomfort does not necessarily make the information useless.

Separate useful feedback from unreasonable demands. Listening does not mean accepting every complaint as correct. Feedback still needs to be assessed fairly.

Customer experience can challenge assumptions. A business may believe that a product or service works well until real users identify difficulties that internal teams have missed.

Failure can provide practical information. Problems show where a process, product or decision did not work as intended.

Keep improving rather than becoming complacent. Positive results can create confidence, while criticism can highlight areas that still need attention.

Ask why something went wrong. The most valuable lesson often comes from understanding the reason behind dissatisfaction rather than simply recording the complaint.

Use feedback to make better decisions. The ultimate value of criticism lies in what an organisation does with the information it receives.

A common misconception about the quote

Complaints are an ordinary part of dealing with people, whether the setting is a shop, a workplace, a technology company or a small service business. Most people would rather hear that something went well than be told where it went wrong. Yet criticism can sometimes provide information that praise does not. A customer who is unhappy has usually encountered a specific problem, and explaining that experience can expose a weakness that others may have overlooked. Bill Gates’ well-known observation about unhappy customers reflects this less comfortable side of learning. It suggests that dissatisfaction should not simply be treated as something to settle and forget. When examined carefully, complaints can show where expectations were missed, assumptions were wrong and changes may be needed.Gates is not suggesting that every unhappy customer is automatically right. Nor does the quote mean that businesses should value complaints more highly than praise. The point is about what dissatisfaction can uncover.A customer who complains has encountered something that did not meet their expectations. If several people report the same problem, the complaint may reveal a weakness that was difficult to see from inside the organisation. A company might believe its website is easy to use, for example, until customers repeatedly struggle to find a basic function. It may think its support service is responsive until users begin describing long waits. The complaint becomes useful because it provides a different perspective.There is also a difference between fixing a complaint and learning from it. A refund may resolve one customer's problem. Understanding why the problem occurred can help prevent hundreds of similar cases.Businesses often have systems designed to measure success. Sales figures, growth, positive reviews and customer retention can all indicate that things are working. But those measures do not necessarily show where the weaknesses are.Unhappy customers tend to point directly towards the rough edges. They may identify something employees have become accustomed to, or a process that made sense when it was designed but no longer works well for the people expected to use it. That makes criticism particularly useful when it is specific. A vague complaint may be difficult to act upon. A detailed account of what went wrong can give a company something concrete to investigate.Bill Gates is best known as the co-founder of Microsoft, the technology company he established with Paul Allen during the early years of the personal computer industry.Born in Seattle in 1955, Gates developed an interest in computing while young. He attended Harvard University but left without completing his degree, choosing instead to focus on Microsoft as the software industry began to expand.Microsoft went on to become one of the world's most influential technology companies. Gates served as its chief executive for many years before gradually moving away from the company's daily management. His career has since included work through the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and a range of interests involving global health, development, climate and technology.A complaint can be treated as an isolated incident, or it can be examined for what it says about the wider system.If customers repeatedly encounter the same difficulty, the issue may not lie with the individual customer. It could be a design problem, an unclear instruction, an inefficient process or a service that has not kept pace with changing expectations. The most useful response is therefore not always the quickest one.A company that simply apologises and closes each case may continue dealing with the same complaint indefinitely. A company that compares complaints and looks for recurring patterns has a better chance of addressing the source.Listening does not mean agreeing with every complaintThere is an important qualification to Gates' idea. Not every complaint represents a genuine flaw. Customers can misunderstand a product, have expectations that were never promised or make demands that a business cannot reasonably meet. Treating every criticism as unquestionable truth can create a different set of problems.The useful approach is to listen carefully and then examine the evidence. Is the complaint isolated? Are other customers describing the same experience? Does the problem appear in usage data or support records? Has the business made an assumption that customers do not share? The value is often found in asking those questions.The idea can apply outside business as well. At work, criticism from a colleague can reveal that a process is unnecessarily complicated. A client questioning a project can expose an assumption that the team had not considered. Even an unsuccessful piece of work can show where communication, timing or planning went wrong.None of this means criticism should be accepted without thought. It means uncomfortable feedback should not automatically be dismissed. Sometimes the person pointing out the problem is also pointing towards the solution.Customer feedback has become much more immediate. Reviews, social media comments, support messages and online discussions can expose problems almost as soon as people encounter them.That creates both an opportunity and a challenge. There is far more feedback available, but not all of it carries equal weight. A single angry comment can attract attention while a quieter pattern of similar complaints goes unnoticed.The important part is identifying what the feedback is actually telling the organisation. A low rating is only a signal. The explanation behind it may be far more useful.Gates' words are sometimes interpreted as if unhappy customers are always the most valuable customers. That is not what the statement means.Satisfied customers provide important information too. They can show which features work, what people appreciate and where a product is meeting expectations. The difference is that dissatisfaction often makes weaknesses easier to see.A satisfied customer confirms that something is working. An unhappy customer may show where it is failing. Both forms of feedback can help a business understand its customers more accurately.
Article Summary: Bill Gates is best known as the co-founder of Microsoft, the technology company he established with Paul Allen during the early years of the personal computer industry. The quote suggests that dissatisfaction should not be treated as something to settle and forget. When examined carefully, complaints can show where expectations were missed, assumptions were wrong and changes may be needed.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos ex-wife MacKenzie Scott who sold half of her Amazon stake has helped abolish $40 billion in medical debt; how mechanics work
Article Text:
Jeff Bezos' ex-wife MacKenzie Scott

How MacKenzie Scott managed to abolish the medical debt of $40 billion

McKenzie Scott’s approach also inspired other billionaires

A model with limits

MacKenzie Scott, ex-wife of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has become one of the most influential philanthropists in America by pioneering large-scale medical debt relief. According to a report by Fortune, through her donations to Undue Medical Debt (formerly known as RIP Medical Debt) Scott helped transform a small non-profit into a national force. Since 2020, her gifts totalling more than. $100 million have enabled the organisation to abolish more than $40 billion medical debt across all 50 states, providing relief to millions of families. The initiative of cutting down the medical debt is a small part of Scott’s larger philanthropic footprint. After her divorce from Bezos, Scott was left with a 4% stake in Amazon which she sold down over time. Scott has also given away more than $26 billion to more than 2,500 organisations which include Black colleges and universities, environmental groups, and economic equity nonprofits and more. As per Fortune report, the recent estimates suggest that her net worth stands at around $33.8 billion.The model introduced by Scott is simple but powerful. The hospitals and physician groups routinely sell uncollectible patient debt in bulk portfolios at steep discounts. Instead of debt collectors buying these portfolios, Undue Medical Debt steps in as the buyer. With donations, it acquires the debt at pennies on the dollar and then abolishes it entirely.The math is striking: every $10 donated erases roughly $1,000 in patient debt. This arbitrage between distressed debt markets and healthcare dysfunction has created one of the most effective philanthropic models in recent years.The model introduced by Scott also inspired other billionaires. Snap co-founder Evan Spiegel and his wife Miranda Kerr recently donated millions to the nonprofit, erasing $550 million in medical bills for 261,000 Californians. Hedge fund billionaire Daniel Och’s family foundation cleared $264 million in Miami-Dade, while New York City and Cook County, Illinois, have used public funds to retire hundreds of millions more. The largest single deal came in April 2025, when Undue Medical Debt retired a $30 billion portfolio, wiping out obligations for 20 million people.Even with Scott's outsized role in scaling the movement, the philanthropic momentum is unfolding against a backdrop of stalled policy reform. A Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule that would have removed medical debt from the credit reports of 15 million Americans was vacated on July 11, 2025, by U.S. District Judge Sean Jordan of the Eastern District of Texas, who ruled it exceeded the CFPB's authority and violated the Fair Credit Reporting Act. No federal medical debt cancellation legislation has advanced through Congress since.That gap between philanthropic scale and policy inaction is central to how critics view the model's limits. Even Undue Medical Debt's $40 billion in total relief, made possible in large part by Scott's early and sustained backing, represents only a fraction of the estimated medical debt held by American households nationwide. Closing that broader gap through voluntary giving alone would likely require a sustained, decades-long commitment, one that also depends on continued access to a distressed debt market that may not always offer the same steep discounts it does today.
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos' ex-wife MacKenzie Scott has become one of the most influential philanthropists in America by pioneering large-scale medical debt relief. Through her donations to Undue Medical Debt, Scott helped transform a small non- profit into a national force. Since 2020, her gifts totalling more than. $100 million have enabled the organisation to abolish more than $40 billion medical debt across all 50 states, providing relief to millions of families.

Article Title: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's 'common sense regulation' may make 'unhappy' Amazon move its delivery operations outside the city
Article Text:
Zohran Mamdani

What the bill Zohran Mamdani is supporting will do

The cost concern

Amazon's warning

Opposition mobilises

A small-business owner's perspective

Where city officials stand

The union's response

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has come up in support of Teamsters-backed bill that would require Amazon and other delivery companies to directly employ thousands of drivers, escalating a fight with the retail giant even as it warns the measure could push its delivery operations out of the five boroughs entirely, according to a New York Post report. Mamdani took to social media platform X to share his opinion of the matter. “If it looks like an Amazon delivery and drives like an Amazon delivery, then it's an Amazon delivery, right? Not according to Amazon. Big companies like Amazon have built a vast network of subcontractors who deliver their packages while shielding them from accountability. It leaves our workers unprotected and our streets less safe. It's time for a change. I'm proud to support the Delivery Protection Act to crack down on exploitative subcontracting and build an economy that works for everyone,” wrote Mamdani.The Delivery Protection Act backed by Mamdani would bar companies from subcontracting core warehouse and delivery work at last-mile facilities, instead requiring those workers to be directly employed by the facility operator. In a statement, the mayor argued that corporations like Amazon have built billion-dollar business models by shielding themselves from accountability through exploitative subcontracting arrangements, and described the measure as "common-sense regulation that protects delivery workers.Critics warn the legislation carries a steep price tag for ordinary New Yorkers. A study by consultancy AKRF found the law could add an extra $664 a year to the cost of deliveries for New York households, a figure that has become central to opposition arguments. A spokesperson for the Business Council of New York State echoed that concern, arguing the law would simply drive up prices for consumers.Amazon, which works with more than 40 local Delivery Service Partners employing over 5,000 people across the city, has said the bill could prompt it to relocate its delivery operations outside city limits altogether. According to AKRF's earlier analysis, such a move would make deliveries both slower and more expensive for residents. An Amazon spokeswoman told the Post the company remains committed to creating good jobs and supporting its employees and small-business partners in New York City, while providing fast and reliable delivery, but said the legislation as written would undercut that commitment by threatening small businesses, putting more than 5,000 jobs at risk, and potentially forcing the company to consider moving delivery operations out of the city.Opponents of the bill organised their own show of force Monday, with delivery workers and small-business owners holding a press conference in East Harlem urging city leaders to reject the measure. The New York Delivers coalition, whose members gathered at Thomas Jefferson Park, argued that the bill, known as Intro 518, threatens thousands of delivery jobs and small businesses while raising costs for city residents. The coalition estimated that as many as 10,000 delivery jobs citywide could be at risk, including roughly 3,500 last-mile delivery jobs concentrated in Harlem and four neighboring council districts. The group also noted that 82% of the last-mile delivery workforce lacks a college degree and 84% is non-white, framing the bill as a threat to a workforce with limited alternative employment options.Rudy Cazares, a New York City native who runs an Amazon Delivery Service Partner and also contracts with FedEx, told the Post the legislation would put him out of business entirely. He said he currently employs around 130 people, with more hired during peak periods like the holidays, and that his drivers start at $23.75 an hour, with experienced drivers earning closer to $27. He emphasised that his employees are all W2 workers, whether full-time or part-time, receiving benefits and having payroll taxes paid on their behalf. Cazares pushed back on the idea that companies like his merely serve as a buffer between Amazon and its drivers, explaining that his company hires its own staff and operates its own vehicles, with Amazon controlling package sorting and staging before his drivers pick them up for delivery. While he acknowledged Amazon pressures its delivery partners to find efficiencies, including through technology, he argued that city officials should address those concerns without eliminating the businesses themselves, saying small businesses like his haven't been part of the conversation shaping the bill.City officials have signaled caution about the bill's potential fallout. Carlos Ortiz, deputy commissioner of external affairs for the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, told an April Council hearing that the city wants to avoid unintended consequences from the measure. A spokesperson for Council Speaker Julie Menin previously said the Manhattan Democrat was allowing the bill to proceed through the legislative process to gather input and engagement from stakeholders before taking a position.A Teamsters union spokesperson pushed back sharply on Amazon's framing of the legislation, arguing that the company would say or do whatever necessary to deny workers stronger rights and wages, and accused journalists of an obligation to scrutinise what the union described as corporate anti-worker messaging rather than simply repeating it. A FedEx spokesperson, meanwhile, noted that last-mile delivery facilities have become an increasingly essential part of the city's logistics infrastructure as e-commerce has grown, and said the company was aware of the bill and working with the New York Delivers coalition, directing further questions on the legislation to that group.
Article Summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has come up in support of a bill that would require Amazon and other delivery companies to directly employ thousands of drivers. The bill would bar companies from subcontracting core warehouse and delivery work at last-mile facilities. Amazon, which works with more than 40 local Delivery Service Partners employing over 5,000 people across the city, has said the bill could prompt it to relocate its delivery operations.

Article Title: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan shares ‘$2-4 billion mistake’ he made because of his job at Microsoft
Article Text:
Passing on the founding role and a $70,000 offer

Tan realises the cost of chasing corporate titles

Tan returned to Palantir as employee number 10

Garry Tan, CEO of startup accelerator Y Combinator, has revealed what he terms a “$2 billion to $4 billion mistake”, which is turning down an early founding role at Palantir Technologies in order to chase a promotion at Microsoft. Speaking on The A16z Show, Tan recounted how close ties during his undergraduate years at Stanford University placed him directly in the orbit of Palantir’s founding team before the data analytics enterprise launched.While studying at Stanford, Tan was a member of the Phi Kappa Psi fraternity alongside future Palantir co-founders Joe Lonsdale and Stephen Cohen. Tan revealed that at the time, both Lonsdale and Cohen were interning at billionaire venture capitalist Peter Thiel’s hedge fund. Following Thiel’s standard recruiting playbook of drafting a list of the smartest engineers to hire for a new venture, both co-founders put Tan on their prospective candidate rosters and flew him from Seattle to meet Thiel over dinner.During the meeting, Thiel made a direct pitch to recruit Tan, offering him a $70,000 upfront check to match the annual salary he was earning as an engineer at Microsoft. Tan declined the opportunity.“I said, 'Thank you very much, Mr. Thiel, but I might get promoted to level 60 this year,’” Tan recalled on the podcast, adding, “Which I did.”With Palantir now valued at approximately $420 billion and trading above $175 per share, which is up sharply from its $10 debut during its 2020 public listing, Tan estimates that turning down a founding-level equity stake cost him between $2 billion and $4 billion.Tan attributed the decision to focusing on conventional prestige rather than trusting exceptional talent and fundamental convictions. He drew a parallel to an earlier career choice where he opted to work on Windows Mobile instead of web development.“Joe and Stephen were among the smartest people I'd ever met. If not them, who was I going to be a cofounder with?,” Tan said.Tan eventually joined Palantir as employee No. 10, though he noted he always regretted not joining during its single-digit founding phase. Tan also shared key takeaways for aspiring founders and software engineers, emphasizing that the most impactful ventures often resemble unconventional subcultures that challenge industry orthodoxies.“Everything that's awesome in my life is kind of a cult,” Tan remarked, adding that groundbreaking startups typically start with “some sort of truth or belief that flies in the face of an orthodoxy. It's very punk, actually.”
Article Summary: Garry Tan, CEO of startup accelerator Y Combinator, has revealed what he terms a ‘$2 billion to $4 billion mistake’ Tan turned down an early founding role at Palantir Technologies in order to chase a promotion at Microsoft.

Article Title: Before playing Mark Zuckerberg in The Social Reckoning, Jeremy Strong sent him an email; Meta CEO replied
Article Text:
Jeremy Strong says he wrote to Mark Zuckerberg before portraying him

Jeremy Strong says he wrote to Mark Zuckerberg

Jeremy Strong says he did not want to 'condemn' Mark Zuckerberg

Jeremy Strong stayed away from Mark Zuckerberg while preparing

The Social Reckoning revisits the Facebook Files

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg received an email from actor Jeremy Strong before filming began for The Social Reckoning, the upcoming movie in which Strong plays the Meta CEO. In a GQ cover story published on August 12, Jeremy Strong said he wanted Mark Zuckerberg to know that he was taking the role seriously and would portray him with respect. He said that Zuckerberg replied to the email, but Strong declined to reveal what the Meta chief wrote back. The film, written by Aaron Sorkin, follows the events surrounding the ‘Facebook Files’ investigation and is scheduled to release on October 9.Speaking to GQ, Strong said he personally reached out to Zuckerberg before production started. “I wrote to him—I’m probably going to give Sony an aneurysm—I sent him an email,” Strong said. He added that the message was meant to reassure Zuckerberg about his approach to the role.“Just to say that I take this responsibility very seriously, and the veracity of it seriously, and I’m approaching it with respect.”Strong confirmed that Zuckerberg replied to the email but chose not to share the contents of his response.Jeremy Strong said his goal was to understand Mark Zuckerberg's point of view instead of judging him.“Listen, I know that he is a reviled person and not a popular person in our culture, but I do not think you should have an actor playing him who wants to set out to condemn him,” he said.He also described portraying the Meta CEO as a major responsibility. “It feels incredibly fraught to talk about the movie, to talk about Mark and being the person who is playing Mark and representing Mark in a sense to the world and to posterity; I feel an enormous sense of weight and responsibility.”Jeremy Strong added: “My job is to understand and defend his point of view and fight his fight.”Although Mark Zuckerberg responded to his email, Jeremy Strong said he likely would not have accepted an invitation to spend time with him at Meta's offices. According to the interview, he prefers researching his characters from a distance instead of closely observing the real people they portray.The actor, who is known for his method acting style, also stayed in character as Zuckerberg throughout filming. Bradley Cooper told GQ that he spoke with Strong several times while he remained in character.“I’ve talked to Mark Zuckerberg many times — I had a whole friendship with Mark Zuckerberg, and Mark Zuckerberg has no idea,” Cooper joked.The Social Reckoning is described as a companion piece to the 2010 film The Social Network. While Jesse Eisenberg played Mark Zuckerberg in the earlier movie, Strong portrays him during the late 2010s and 2020.The film focuses on The Wall Street Journal's Facebook Files investigation and whistleblower Frances Haugen's allegations about Facebook's internal practices. Zuckerberg defended the company in 2021, saying claims that Facebook deliberately promoted content that made people angry for profit were "deeply illogical." The Social Reckoning is scheduled to arrive in theatres on October 9.
Article Summary: Jeremy Strong said he wanted Mark Zuckerberg to know that he was taking the role seriously and would portray him with respect. He said that Zuckerberg replied to the email, but Strong declined to reveal what the Meta chief wrote back. The Social Reckoning follows the events surrounding the ‘Facebook Files’ investigation.

Article Title: Why some Anthropic investors call CEO Dario Amodei 'more of a religious leader than he is a CEO'
Article Text:
The Anthropic IPO is a referendum on whether CEO Dario Amodei doom sells to public investors

Inside Anthropic, a tiny inner circle and a company that asks Claude first

CEO Dario Amodei's AI safety stance has cost Anthropic money

Somebody in the room had a perfectly reasonable idea. Anthropic was mid-way through a historic run, public sentiment around AI was in the gutter, and one director suggested the fix that Microsoft and Facebook reached for during their own boom years—a charm offensive, heavy on drug discovery and cures for hard diseases. Dario Amodei said no. That approach belonged to the past, he argued. The stakes now were more existential.That exchange, reported by The Information, works almost as a thesis statement for how Amodei runs the fastest-growing major company in history. Weeks later, Anthropic's World Cup commercial opened on a row of tombstones and told viewers to ask hard questions about AI. Now, with an IPO expected as soon as September, the 43-year-old has to take that same posture on the road—to money managers who, according to the report, would very much like him to stop frightening everyone.The discomfort isn't new, it's just newly consequential. One Silicon Valley investor wrote down an unusual risk before putting money into Anthropic: he wasn't convinced Amodei actually cared about making money. Others have complained privately that his campaign for AI regulation damages both his company and the wider industry. They also concede they have almost no sway over him.Bill Gurley, who hasn't invested, has called it the most aggressive regulatory capture he's seen.Amodei's allies read the criticism differently—Brad Carson, who runs an Anthropic-backed nonprofit, argues the loudest critics are the ones who can't replicate what he built.Few people close to the company could name a meaningful influence on Amodei beyond his sister and president Daniela, his five other co-founders, and his wife Camilla Clark, a former tech operator with almost no public profile who has never held a role at Anthropic. He leads through long essays and Slack posts, skips most day-to-day management, and holds a twice-monthly all-hands that staff call Dario's Vision Quests—less product review, more state of the world.Employees lean on Claude itself for decisions. Headcount sits above 3,000 and executives don't plan to raise it much, because they'd rather not hire people they'll later have to cut as Claude absorbs internal work. One major investor's summary, per The Information: he is "more of a religious leader than he is a CEO."The conviction has a price tag. When bioweapon classifiers began eating into model margins, the finance team objected and Amodei overruled them. His refusal to accept a Pentagon requirement on permitted uses got Anthropic designated a supply chain risk in March. In June, after a dispute over Fable 5's guardrails, Washington slapped export controls on the model and forced it offline for days.None of it has dented the ascent. Anthropic's valuation has climbed more than 200-fold in three years to $965 billion, and its revenue run rate—estimated recently at $70 billion—passed OpenAI's earlier this year.The compromises are real too: money from Qatar and the UAE, over $1 billion a month paid to Elon Musk's SpaceX for compute. Amodei's own framing, from his January essay, explains the bind better than his critics do. AI, he wrote, is "such a glittering prize" that restraint becomes nearly impossible.
Article Summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's stance on AI has cost the company money. The company's valuation has climbed more than 200-fold in three years to $965 billion. One Silicon Valley investor wrote down an unusual risk before putting money into Anthropic. Others have complained privately that his campaign for AI regulation damages his company.

Article Title: A robot traveled to Great Pyramid via hidden path and stopped in front of a door that had remained sealed for 4,500 years; here's what happened
Article Text:
Robot explores hidden passage inside Great Pyramid

What did the robot find

Modern technology used to study pyramids

A robot traveled through a hidden passage inside Egypt’s Great Pyramid of Giza and stopped at a sealed barrier that may have remained untouched for about 4,500 years. The discovery has renewed questions about what could be hidden inside the ancient monument. According to an online report, researchers used modern robotic and scanning technology to explore a narrow passage that would be difficult and risky for people to enter. The robot reached the end of the corridor but found a solid wall or sealed doorway. Archaeologists say further study could reveal new details about the pyramid’s design and construction.The Great Pyramid of Giza has been studied for centuries, but scientists still do not know everything about its internal structure. Rob Richardson, Professor of Robotics at Leeds, and his small team accepted the challenge in 2020 of exploring a narrow shaft inside the pyramid. The project began after Hong Kong dentist and inventor Dr. Tze Chuen Ng challenged researchers to design a robot that could travel through the passage and investigate what lay beyond it.The shaft measures just 20 cm by 20 cm and stretches about 60 metres (197 feet). Earlier attempts to explore it had damaged the passage, making it important for the team to design a robot that could move through it without causing further harm.The project took almost five years to complete.Richardson and his team developed a lightweight robot that weighed about 5 kg. Its small size and low weight allowed it to move through the narrow passage while using relatively little power.“This design was certainly challenging,” Richardson said. “The robot had to be extremely lightweight – and in the end, we got it down to 5kg.”He added: “Because it was so light, it did not require a lot of power – in the end, the challenges started to become opportunities.”The team also developed a system that allowed the robot to move gently through the shaft.“We developed a system that moved the robot very gently through the passageway,” Richardson said.The robot's camera eventually provided researchers with a view of an area that had remained inaccessible.Instead of finding an open chamber, the robot reached a solid wall or sealed door. The finding has not answered the biggest question surrounding the passage. It has instead created a new one: What is behind the sealed barrier?The area has not been opened, and there has been no confirmed public announcement about what may be on the other side. Egyptologist Zahi Hawass has said that he plans to issue an official report on findings related to the passage after 2026.He has also suggested that a breakthrough of a discovery could radically change our understanding of ancient Egypt.Researchers have increasingly turned to technology to study the Great Pyramid without damaging its ancient stonework. Scientists have used techniques such as thermal imaging, 3D mapping and muon scanning to look inside the massive structure.
Article Summary: Researchers used modern robotic and scanning technology to explore a narrow passage that would be difficult and risky for people to enter. The robot reached the end of the corridor but found a solid wall or sealed doorway. Archaeologists say further study could reveal new details about the pyramid’s design and construction.

Article Title: Google Gemini 3.7 Flash launched for coding, agents: Everything the upgraded model offers
Article Text:
Google has launched Gemini 3.7 flash

Lower API pricing and Google Workspace upgrades

Google has launched Gemini 3.7 Flash, its latest AI model optimised specifically for complex software engineering tasks, web development and autonomous agent workflows. The newest model arrived three weeks after the release of Gemini 3.6 Flash, and the company says that it introduces substantial performance gains in multi-step planning, instruction following and code generation, while debuting at half the per-token introductory price of its predecessor.Major Gains in Coding, Web Design, and Document AnalysisAccording to benchmark results released by Google, Gemini 3.7 Flash delivers marked improvements over the 3.6 model across several technical domains. The company claims that the updated model achieved higher first-pass code accuracy and produced more production-ready code, scoring 43.6% on FrontierCode 1.1 (up from 34.4%) and 65.3% on DeepSWE v1.1 (up from 49.0%).It also said that in UI and web application design, the model demonstrated stronger layout functionality and reference-matching accuracy, earning an Elo score of 1588 compared to 3.6 Flash's 1538 on Arena.ai's WebDev Arena. For complex data processing, for fields like finance, law, and biosciences, Gemini 3.7 Flash significantly outperformed the previous version on document-processing evaluations and real-world business automation tasks.To boost enterprise adoption and scalable deployment of autonomous agents, Google is offering Gemini 3.7 Flash at an introductory price of $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens through the end of the year. The company noted that the model is designed to “think more diligently,” requiring less manual developer oversight, fewer retries, and offering better execution during multi-step tool calls.Alongside developer availability via Google's API channels, Gemini 3.7 Flash is being integrated immediately into Gemini Spark, Google's 24/7 personal AI agent available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in over 160 countries. The update is expected to improve Spark's execution across Google Workspace applications, enhancing accuracy in complex, multi-app workflows.
Article Summary: Google has launched Gemini 3.7 Flash, its latest AI model optimised specifically for complex software engineering tasks, web development and autonomous agent workflows. The newest model arrived three weeks after the release of Gemini. 3.6 Flash, and the company says that it introduces substantial performance gains in multi-step planning, instruction following and code generation.
